html:
Hip hop is a music and culture born at block parties in the Bronx, New York, in the 1970s. Its music, rap, grew into the most popular genre on earth.

The Bronx then was poor and burning, its neighbourhoods cut apart by highways and neglect. In August 1973 DJ Kool Herc, a young man from Jamaica, threw a party where he played only the drum "breaks" of funk records, looping them on two turntables. He borrowed the big sound systems of Jamaican reggae. Dancers and rhymers took over the breaks.

Hip hop came to have four parts:

  • DJing, cutting and mixing records
  • MCing, or rapping, rhyming over the beat
  • breakdancing
  • graffiti art

Grandmaster Flash and Afrika Bambaataa built on Herc's work. "Rapper's Delight" by the Sugarhill Gang (1979) was the first big hit. Through the 1980s and 1990s artists such as Run DMC, Public Enemy and many others took it from the streets to the charts, and rap became a voice for young Black Americans.

By the late 2010s hip hop was the most listened to music in the United States, and local scenes thrived from Lagos to Seoul.
sum: Hip hop is a music and culture born at block parties in the Bronx, New York, in the 1970s. Its music, rap, grew into the most popular genre on earth.
